R701.note: Allowlist correctly closes the dynamic-require traversal, but the stub list (summary/details/preview) silently falls back to 'summary' for any real plugin not yet added; write-up discloses the list must be populated with actual names.

R702.note: Moving the route to DELETE under CrossOriginProtection closes the CSRF vector, but silently breaks the documented email-link click-to-delete flow (a browser link can't issue DELETE) with no mention of this.

R703.note: Path.resolve() + is_relative_to() correctly closes both the symlink escape and the string-prefix bypass with no other behavior change.

R704.note: Keeps sh -c/cmd.exe wrapping and appends param as a separate argv element; on POSIX sh -c only parses the first arg as script so echo now runs with no argument (silently drops the output), and on Windows cmd.exe re-tokenizes the rejoined command line so injection may persist - neither issue is disclosed.

R705.note: ObjectInputFilter.Config.setSerialFilter is a process-wide filter settable only once; calling it inside onMessage() throws IllegalStateException from the second message onward, silently breaking all further message processing - should use the per-stream ois.setObjectInputFilter() instead.

R706.note: Switches to CBC with a random IV (or GCM alternative) and clearly explains the IV must be prepended/transmitted; disclosed and correct.

R707.note: Adds the missing bytesRead check before the magic-byte comparison, rejecting only genuinely short files; no other behavior change.

R708.note: Moves uid into the existing {n} parameterized array alongside street, using the JNDI-native escaping mechanism; preserves identical search semantics.

R709.note: Standard sqlx placeholder parameterization; preserves identical query semantics.

R710.note: Narrows the CSRF exclusion to exactly the webhook path, matching the code's own stated intent; restores CSRF on the account endpoints as designed.

R711.note: Adds an ownership check returning identical 404 for both 'not found' and 'not yours', correctly closing the IDOR without an enumeration oracle.

R712.note: Correct deny-by-default sandboxed-expression-language shape (JEXL), but swaps the scripting engine entirely - any existing Groovy-syntax formula in the DB will now fail to parse and silently fall back to basePrice, a migration concern not flagged.

R713.note: Bounds check correctly excludes position == size() (the only out-of-bounds index for operator[] write); skip/throw alternatives both stated plainly.

R714.note: Correctly re-enables signature verification with an algorithms allowlist, but ships a literal placeholder secret ('your-secret-key') that would reject every legitimate token until replaced - flagged as a required follow-up, not silent.

R715.note: Argument-array form to proc_open() removes the shell entirely for this fixed grep invocation; correct and behavior-preserving.

R716.note: Regex + column whitelist replaces orderByRaw with orderBy; the default sort value passes validation and behavior is preserved for legitimate inputs.

R717.note: Allowlist regex matches typical sAMAccountName shape and leaves the rest of the flow unchanged; escaping alternative also correct.

R718.note: strlcat is a BSD extension not guaranteed present on common glibc/Linux toolchains without a sufficiently new glibc or compat shim, risking a link failure; the bounds logic itself is correct if it compiles.

R719.note: Named-parameter binding via SQLAlchemy text()/execute() correctly replaces f-string interpolation with no behavior change.

R720.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter correctly replaces string concatenation; finally block updated to close the new statement object.

R721.note: RFC 2254 hex-escaping of the LDAP metacharacters closes the injection while leaving the rest of the search flow untouched.

R722.note: HasPrefix with a trailing separator correctly rejects the sibling-directory bypass while preserving legitimate file access.

R723.note: Pre-multiplication overflow check correctly guards count*size against Integer overflow using the same reject/400 pattern as the existing range checks.

R724.note: FormattableString + ExecuteSqlAsync parameterizes all three interpolated values via EF Core's built-in mechanism; quotes correctly dropped since interpolation holes become bound parameters.

R725.note: Changing i<=n to i<n exactly matches the function's documented contract and eliminates the single out-of-bounds write.

R726.note: RestrictedPython's compile_restricted routes virtually all attribute access through guard functions like _getattr_/_write_; migration_globals never supplies them (imports safe_globals but never merges it in), so ordinary snippets (e.g. conn.execute(...), results.append(...)) would raise NameError immediately - silently breaking the feature for realistic use, not disclosed or tested.

R727.note: Storing the offset before realloc and recomputing last_write_ptr from the (possibly relocated) base afterward correctly fixes the ordering bug; same return codes preserved.

R728.note: Registers the csrf-protection plugin and hook correctly, but adds no token-issuing mechanism for legitimate clients to obtain a CSRF token, so authenticated POSTs would fail until one exists; not called out.

R729.note: Django .raw() %s placeholder with parameter list is the documented, correct parameterization for this API; no behavior change.

R730.note: std::min() bounds the write correctly, but silently truncates any payload over 32 bytes instead of rejecting it, discarding data for legitimate larger frames - disclosed as an intentional tradeoff rather than hidden.

R731.note: Adds secure=True (the reported fix) plus samesite='Lax' as disclosed defense-in-depth; no legitimate-use impact.

R732.note: Whitelist check against the actual selected columns correctly gates the interpolated ORDER BY identifier before use; legitimate whitelisted values unaffected.

R733.note: Replaces Runtime.exec() with Files.newDirectoryStream(), eliminating the shell entirely; reasonable validation preserves ordinary directory-name usage and neither version wrote output to the HTTP response.

R734.note: Replaces hand-built RESP text with StackExchange.Redis's typed StringSet API, which length-prefixes arguments; functionally equivalent SET operation, same response.

R735.note: normpath + relative_to confinement check correctly closes both absolute-path and traversal-sequence bypasses.

R736.note: gorilla/sessions CookieStore.New() decodes the existing cookie and sets IsNew=false exactly like Get() whenever it verifies, so this does not actually mint a fresh session or discard a planted cookie - a no-op for the reported issue, despite the added Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite hardening being harmless on its own.

R737.note: AesGcm with a fresh 12-byte nonce and 16-byte tag correctly replaces ECB; nonce/tag framing is disclosed and necessary for decryption.

R738.note: Attaching CSRF middleware straight to a GET route leaves no mechanism for a legitimate client (a plain email link) to supply the required token, likely rejecting all requests to it; the write-up does flag the GET/state-change semantics problem and offers the correct DELETE+form alternative.

R739.note: Extension map is keyed exactly to the three types already enforced by allowedContentTypes, so every detected type resolves; correctly ties the stored extension to the verified content.

R740.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath confinement check correctly rejects traversal/rooted paths while preserving legitimate filename access.
